scenario: 今日具身智能这一侧，力、空间关系和评测效率被同时拿出来讨论。有的给触觉和力度搭起可复用的采集与评测栈，有的让策略按当前负载规划并在接触变化时稳住出力。全身运动先验被用来协调人形行走和操作，三维关系图和空间预见则用来补上视觉-语言-动作模型里常被隐含掉的几何。安全过滤器不再只在测试时改动作，训练也会为干预后的状态做准备。人类玩法可以在没有机器人动作标签时先学技能，而大规模真机评测开始用自动出题和打分减少人工复位。还有工作把关键动作和密集运动拆开，或从操作过程本身抽出该看哪里的感知监督。

papers.title: Tacinf: A Unified Tactile Infrastructure for Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Qiwei Wu, Xiangyu Chen, Xin Xiang, Rui Zhang, Yihang Kang, Weiran Chen, Zikang Xie, Yangfan Li, Tao Wang, Xiangzheng Wang, Tianyi Bi, Zhiyan Zhang, Xianpeng Wang, Mingqian Zhou, Yan Yu, Chuanyu Li, Wenjie Zhang, Tao Li, Weihua Zhang, Renjing Xu, Junjie Lai
papers.summary: 要按任务和触觉来控制力度，机器人往往缺少一套低成本、可复用的数据与评测工具。新的模块化基础设施把仿真合成、触觉基准、视觉-触觉-语言-动作策略、手持采集和仿真到真机评测串成一条工作流，任务指令还可以指定力度。只在触觉仿真数据上微调的基础模型，能够零样本转到不同的真机任务。在物体位置和实例都随机时，把遥操作、仿真和手持采集数据混在一起，真机平均成功率从只用遥操作时的 20% 提高到 60%。在两种力度指令下，实测握力也会按要求分开。
papers.abstract: Force-aware manipulation requires robots to infer appropriate interaction forces from task context and tactile feedback. We present Tacinf, a low-cost, modular infrastructure that enables policies to predict robot actions and fingertip forces from task language, vision, and touch. Task instructions can optionally specify the desired force level. Tacinf integrates simulation data synthesis and tactile benchmarking (Tabero), vision-tactile-language-action (VTLA) policy learning, handheld data collection using the same gripper as robot deployment (Tacumi), and task-aligned sim-to-real evaluation (Taco). Together, these components form an integrated workflow connecting data collection from multiple sources, foundation-model training, and hardware deployment. We validate each component, including the simulation data, benchmark, controller, and Tacumi, and are releasing the full stack as open source. A foundation model fine-tuned solely on tactile simulation data transfers zero-shot to different real-robot tasks. Across eight policy variants, mean task success rates are strongly correlated between simulation and the real robot (Pearson r=0.998, mean maximum rank violation MMRV=0.010). For the four policies with reported force measurements, mean grip force is higher under firm instructions than under gentle instructions on all three tasks in both domains. When both object positions and instances are randomized, a mixture of teleoperation, simulation, and Tacumi data raises mean real-robot task success from 20% with teleoperation alone to 60%.

papers.title: Force2Act: A Force-Aware Visuomotor Policy for Generalizable Compliant Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Keerthi Vasan Murugan, Fangguo Zhao, Jiafei Duan
papers.summary: 接触丰富的操作不但要走到正确位置，还得把出力控制住。现有力度策略多从演示里学习，演示里没出现过的更大负载，上线后就跟不上。新方法先按当前测到的相互作用，为一段动作规划相对力度，再在规划间隙用一组力度专家在每个控制步上选对调节器，使接触变化时仍能稳住。它在五个接触任务的仿真基准上总体成功率达到 93.8%，最强对照是 77.0%。在真机四项任务上平均成功率为 94.2%，对照最高只有 27.5%。
papers.abstract: Contact-rich manipulation requires a robot to regulate the force it applies, not only where it moves. Existing force-aware policies learn this force from demonstrations and therefore reproduce the force levels they were trained on, which fails once the interaction demands more force than any demonstration. We present Force2Act, a hybrid force-position policy built on two complementary mechanisms. A global force policy plans the motion and the interaction force once per action chunk, with force represented relative to the measured interaction, so that the planned force scales with the load. Between planning steps, a reactive compliance policy, termed Mixture of Force Experts, identifies at every control step the force expert that governs the interaction and regulates the force through it, so that the contact holds when it changes within a chunk. We further introduce Force2Act-Bench, a simulation benchmark of five contact-rich tasks that gives the community a common and repeatable way to test force-aware policies and measure how well they regulate the interaction force. Force2Act achieves an overall success rate of 93.8%, compared with 77.0% for the strongest baseline, and its reactive regulation reduces the failures on block pivoting from 30 to 10 of 150 trials. On a real robot, Force2Act reaches an average success rate of 94.2% over four tasks, against at most 27.5% for the baselines.

papers.title: CHAMP: Coordinated Humanoid Loco-Manipulation with Whole-Body Motion Priors
papers.authors: Lijun Han, Muyuan Ma, Zichen Wang, Siyuan Liu, Yuxi Liu, Yutong Wang, Bohao Zhang, Heng Zhou, Wei Sui
papers.summary: 人形机器人要在人的环境里同时走路和用手做事，难点是从杂乱数据里学到全身运动先验，再把它用到协调控制上。新方法用大约两千小时的人类和机器人数据，预训练视觉语言模型去预测未来的身体和手部运动，再用面向协调的动作专家从预训练模型的多层特征里稀疏选出身体和手的动作。在七项仿真任务上总体成功率为 84.8%，在 Unitree G1 的七项真机任务上为 91.4%，都超过所比较的基线。长程爆米花递送任务上，成功率为 70.0%，最强对照是 40.0%。
papers.abstract: Coordinating locomotion and dexterous manipulation is fundamental to humanoid robots operating in human environments. A key challenge is learning motion priors from diverse data and using them effectively for coordinated robot control. We present CHAMP, a unified framework for humanoid loco-manipulation that combines whole-body motion pretraining with adaptive feature extraction. CHAMP pretrains a vision-language model to predict future body and hand motion from approximately 2,298 hours of heterogeneous human and robot data. A shared motion representation enables unified whole-body motion learning across embodiments from datasets with body annotations, hand annotations, or both. To ground these motion priors in robot control, we introduce a Coordination-oriented Action Expert (CAE) and train it on replay data generated using the target controller. Through sparse routing, CAE adaptively selects, transforms, and fuses features from multiple layers of the pretrained model to jointly generate body and hand actions. In experiments, CHAMP achieves overall success rates of 84.8% on seven simulated tasks and 91.4% on seven real-world tasks with a Unitree G1, outperforming the evaluated baselines in both settings. In particular, CHAMP achieves 70.0% success on the long-horizon popcorn-serving task, compared with 40.0% for the best-performing baseline.

papers.title: WeaveVLA: 3D Relational Grounding for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.authors: Zien Wang, Yuhao Pan, Yunfeng Fan, Nan Cheng, Xin Xia, Wenchao Xu
papers.summary: 视觉-语言-动作模型虽然能按指令控制机器人，但对任务相关的三维关系、以及这些关系在操作中如何变化，通常只是隐含在表示里。新方法用任务条件的稀疏图网络显式编码物体、夹爪和附近参照之间的相对三维关系，并用循环边状态把多帧几何证据串起来，再读成关系 token 去调节动作。它在两个主干上，LIBERO 平均成功率都超过 98%。在三项真机任务上，基于 StarVLA-GR00T 的版本把标准条件下的平均成功率从 55.6% 提高到 70.0%，分布外扰动下也有明显提升。
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models leverage pretrained vision-language representations for instruction-conditioned robot control, yet their understanding of task-relevant 3D relations and how these relations evolve during manipulation remains largely implicit. To address this challenge, we introduce \textbf{WeaveVLA}, a framework that enhances VLA action generation by explicitly modeling task-relevant relative 3D relations and maintaining relational context across observations. WeaveVLA employs a task-conditioned sparse graph neural network to encode relative 3D relations among objects, the gripper, and nearby references. Pair-specific recurrent edge states integrate geometric evidence across observations to maintain evolving spatial context. A learned-query readout summarizes the updated graph representations into compact relational tokens, which condition the action expert alongside the original vision-language context. An auxiliary geometry reconstruction objective further encourages spatial structure preservation. We instantiate WeaveVLA on StarVLA-GR00T and $\pi_{0.5}$, achieving over 98\% average success on LIBERO with both backbones. On LIBERO-Plus, WeaveVLA improves success from 74.9\% to 82.0\% and from 85.7\% to 87.8\%, respectively, with additional improvements on CALVIN D$\rightarrow$D. On three real-world tasks, the StarVLA-GR00T-based variant improves average success from 55.6\% to 70.0\% under standard conditions and from 33.3\% to 53.3\% under OOD perturbations, surpassing the $\pi_{0.5}$ baseline in both settings.

papers.title: Intervention-Robust VLA: Diverse Demonstrations for Robot Deployment with Safety Filters
papers.authors: Tzu-Yuan Huang, Shao-Hsuan Chang, Dai-Jie Wu, Ralf Römer, Yung-Hui Li, Stefan Sosnowski, Angela P. Schoellig, Kenneth Marino, Sandra Hirche
papers.summary: 部署时的安全过滤器会改掉不安全动作，却也可能把机器人推到训练很少见到的状态，任务成功率跟着掉下来。直接从数据里学安全行为，又很难覆盖所有关键场景。新方法在同样的数据预算下，加入多样化且能完成任务的演示，扩大任务相关状态覆盖，让训练分布更接近带安全过滤的部署。真机实验里，它在分布内和分布外都保持安全，并把名义策略的安全成功率从 0% 提高到最多 90%。在两个被评估的视觉-语言-动作模型上，都稳定好于只用常规数据训练。
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) have shown strong potential for learning complex robotic behaviors from demonstrations. However, learning safe behavior directly from data requires extensive coverage of safety-critical situations, which is often impractical in real-world settings. Test-time safety filters provide an alternative by correcting unsafe actions during deployment, but these interventions can drive the robot into states poorly covered by the training data, thereby degrading task performance. We introduce InteR-VLA, an intervention-robust framework for VLAs that leverages diverse task-completing demonstrations to broaden task-relevant state coverage and maintain competence under safety interventions. By better aligning the training distribution with safety-filtered deployment under the same data budget, our approach mitigates intervention-induced distribution shift while preserving task performance. Real-world experiments across in-distribution and out-of-distribution settings show that InteR-VLA maintains safety, increases Safe Success Rate up to 90% from 0% for nominal policies, and consistently outperforms nominal-data training on both evaluated VLAs.

papers.title: Foresight Forcing: Learning Spatial Foresight for Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors: Mishuo Han, Zhixuan Liang, Zhaoyuan Wan, Wendi Chen, Jiarui Chen, Xinkai Wang, Yue Ma, Yu Zhou, Junting Chen, Yao Mu, Jun Lv, Chuan Wen, Cewu Lu
papers.summary: 操作策略如果能预见到物体怎么动、空间关系怎么变，动作往往会更稳，但现有世界动作模型通常只预测未来图像，三维几何变化仍是隐含的。新方法在训练时用冻结的三维基础模型，从对齐的当前和未来观察里提取特征差，作为几何感知的监督，再把这些目标蒸馏进空间转移查询。部署时不必再看未来观察，也不调用那个三维教师。它在 LIBERO 和 RoboTwin2.0 上表现更稳健，后者完整设置的平均成功率为 95.01%。在六项真机操作任务上，平均任务得分达到 85.8%。
papers.abstract: Robotic manipulation policies can improve action prediction by anticipating how objects move and how their spatial relationships change. World Action Models (WAMs) learn to predict future visual observations, but their training objectives typically leave the underlying 3D geometric transitions implicit. To alleviate this problem, we introduce Foresight Forcing ($\mathcal{F}^{2}$), a WAM that learns a spatial transition representation from changes in a pretrained 3D feature space. During training, a frozen 3D foundation model extracts patch-wise feature differences from aligned current and future observations that provide dense supervision for geometry-aware feature transitions. We distill these targets into spatial transition queries, which are progressively refined from the current observation, language instruction, and proprioceptive state, and use them alongside current visual features to generate actions. At deployment, the policy predicts the queries without future observations or the 3D teacher. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin2.0 demonstrate strong manipulation performance and improved robustness, including 95.01% average success on RoboTwin2.0 Full. On six real-world manipulation tasks, $\mathcal{F}^{2}$ achieves a mean task score of 85.8%.

papers.title: DiWALI: Diffusion Policy Learning in World Models via Latent Action Inference from Human and Robot Play
papers.authors: Akshay L Chandra, Iman Nematollahi, Lingyue Zhao, Daria Kulikova, Angela P. Schoellig, Fabien Despinoy, Abhinav Valada
papers.summary: 机器人操作数据带动作标注的很少，人类玩法或视频虽然多，却没有对应的机器人动作。新方法用逆动力学模型从相邻帧推断潜在动作，先在没有动作标签的数据上训练世界模型，再用机器人玩法单独训练一个解码器，把潜在动作落到真实指令上。技能策略先在无动作标注的人类演示上学习，再在想象中用强化学习改进。在 CALVIN 基准上，只靠人类演示训练的策略明显超过用机器人演示训练的对照。加入人类玩法后，世界模型微调出的策略也强于只用同样数量的机器人玩法。
papers.abstract: Learning robot manipulation is constrained by the availability of action-labeled robot data, for both imitation and world models. Humans can demonstrate skills in seconds, but their demonstrations lack the required robot actions. We introduce DiWALI, a framework that learns and improves diffusion policies within a world model trained on human and robot play. DiWALI infers latent actions from consecutive frames using an inverse dynamics model, enabling world model training without action labels, and grounds them in robot commands through a decoder trained separately on robot play. Skill policies are trained over latent actions from action-free human demonstrations and improved with reinforcement learning in imagination. On the CALVIN benchmark, DiWALI policies trained solely from human demonstrations substantially outperform baselines trained with robot demonstrations. Incorporating human play into the world model training also yields stronger policies after fine-tuning than using the same amount of robot play alone. Experiments on a physical robot show that skills learned primarily from human demonstrations are further improved in imagination with a world model trained on human and robot play. Together, these results demonstrate that human experience can support both manipulation skill acquisition and subsequent policy improvement, reducing reliance on action-labeled robot data. Videos, dataset and code are available at https://diwali.cs.uni-freiburg.de.

papers.title: ScaleEvals: Scaling Generalist Policy Evaluation through Reset-Free Autonomous Play
papers.authors: Amitoj Sandhu, Ethan Sick, Omkaar Buddhikot, Nadia Laswi, Wesley Durbano, Nadun Ranawaka, You Liang Tan
papers.summary: 评通用机器人策略，往往要靠人来复位、打分，任务集又小，很难看出能力短板。新协议让一组机器人连续自主对打，用视觉语言模型根据现场生成带难度和技能标签的任务，再用另一个模型给进度打分，与人工评分的一致率为 90.7%。在 DROID 和 YAM 上超过三千次真机回放中，每个工位每小时净完成 23.0 次，主动人工劳动减少 98%。由此排出的五个通用策略名次，与留出的人工评测高度一致，还能用已有证据预测未见提示上的名次变化。
papers.abstract: Real-world evaluation of generalist robot policies is bottlenecked by manual resets, human grading, and small fixed task suites with limited diagnostic coverage. We present ScaleEvals, a scalable reset-free protocol that evaluates policies through continuous physical play across a robot fleet. A VLM AutoPrompter generates scene-grounded tasks with difficulty estimates, language prompts, and skill tags, enabling performance analysis across diverse rollouts. A VLM AutoGrader assesses task progress, achieving 90.7% agreement with human graders. Scores are aggregated via a soft-win Bradley-Terry model, while tag-stratified ANOVA provides interpretable capability diagnostics. Across 3,000+ physical autonomous rollouts on DROID and YAM, ScaleEvals achieves 23.0 net rollouts/hr per station while reducing active human labor by 98%. By ranking five SOTA generalist policies, ScaleEvals correlates with held-out manual evaluation ranking on DROID (r=0.94, rho=0.90, p=0.018), and remains internally consistent on a second embodiment, YAM (r=0.839, rho=0.80). Beyond aggregate rankings, we observe behavioral compositionality: recombining verb-, skill-, and object-conditioned evidence predicts policy order on unseen prompts. Across 10 tasks and 240 prospective physical rollouts, we recover three-policy orderings of 96% pairwise concordance, demonstrating ScaleEvals can predict not just which policy leads, but where rankings reverse.

papers.title: H-VLA: Hierarchical Vision-Language-Action Model with Key-Action Reasoning and Motion Planning in a Unified Action Space
papers.authors: Xiongfeng Peng, Lu Xu, Yandong Wang, Jiaqian Yu, Zirui Zheng, Yamin Mao, Weiming Li, Inseop Chung, Hyun-woong Cho, Jaewook Yoo, Dongwook Lee, Daehyun Ji, Chao Zhang
papers.summary: 不少视觉-语言-动作模型仍把语言和图像直接映射成密集动作，预训练里学到的语义推理容易被冲掉，物体位置、场景、本体和相机一变就更脆。新方法把高层关键动作推理和底层运动生成拆开：先预测下一步子目标，再据此生成密集动作，并用统一的相机坐标系动作空间贯通不同数据、本体和视角。在 SimplerEnv 上，Google Robot 视觉匹配成功率为 91%，变体聚合为 84%。在 Agilex 真机上，相对最强对照，分布外位置提高 47 个百分点，分布内和分布外场景或物体上也有提升。
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown strong potential for robotic manipulation, but many existing methods still rely on direct mappings from language and visual observations to dense actions. This formulation can weaken the semantic reasoning capability inherited from pre-trained Vision-Language Models (VLMs), which are mainly optimized for visual-linguistic understanding rather than low-level control, and becomes fragile under spatial variations, including changes in object positions, scene layouts, robot embodiments, and camera viewpoints. To address these limitations, we propose H-VLA, a hierarchical VLA framework that decouples high-level key-action reasoning from low-level motion generation. H-VLA combines a Key-Action Model for predicting a key-action as the next manipulation subgoal, a Motion Planning Model for generating dense future actions conditioned on the predicted key-action, and a Unified Camera-Centric Action Space for consistent representation across datasets, embodiments, and viewpoints. We further adopt a two-stage training strategy that emphasizes key-action reasoning during pre-training and dense motion generation during fine-tuning. Experiments show that H-VLA achieves strong performance on SimplerEnv, reaching 91% on Google Robot visual matching, 84% on Google Robot variant aggregation, and 81% on WidowX visual matching. On Agilex real-robot tasks, H-VLA improves over the strongest baseline by 10, 47, and 16 percentage points under in-distribution, out-of-distribution position, and out-of-distribution scene/object settings, respectively.

papers.title: A³-VLA: Automatic Perception-Guided Attention Alignment for Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Shengzhe Zhang, Qi Zhang, Dazhong Shen, Chao Wang, Shaopeng Zhai, Hui Xiong
papers.summary: 视觉-语言-动作模型在学动作时，往往缺少细粒度的感知监督，容易把注意力放到和任务无关的视觉捷径上，偏离目标物体和关键交互区域。新方法从操作过程中的视觉变化出发，先得到目标和机器人的候选区域，再用分割模型离线精修，并配上两项训练目标：让语言或机器人状态查询视觉时把足够注意力分给任务关键区域，同时把候选目标区域的表示与语言对齐、与无关区域分开。在仿真和真机操作任务上，它能稳定提升多种主干，平均成功率提高 6.5% 到 25.2%。
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action Models (VLAs) enable robots to perform manipulation tasks by leveraging Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to process visual observations and language instructions. However, the action prediction objective itself lacks fine-grained task-specific perceptual supervision, making it prone to relying on task-irrelevant visual shortcuts, leading attention away from target objects and key interaction areas, thereby limiting its operational performance and generalization ability. To address this, we propose Automatic Perception-Guided Attention Alignment for Robot Manipulation ($\text{A}^3$-VLA), a framework that derives task-specific visual guidance from the manipulation process itself. Specifically, $\text{A}^3$-VLA first generates heuristic candidate regions for target objects and the robot from interaction-induced visual changes, and refines them with a visual segmentation model offline. These regions serve as explicit perceptual guidance through two complementary objectives: an attention allocation loss that encourages sufficient focus on task-critical regions when language or robot state tokens query the visual input, and a contrastive learning loss that aligns the representations of candidate target regions with language instructions while separating them from task-irrelevant regions. Extensive experiments on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks demonstrate that $\text{A}^3$-VLA consistently improves multiple VLA backbones, with an average success rate gain of 6.5% - 25.2% across benchmarks.
